name: Isolated Focal Cortical Dysplasia Type IIa

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Classification for Focal Cortical Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of dysmorphic neurons without balloon cells on histopathological examination
Focal epilepsy with onset typically in childhood or adolescence
MRI evidence of focal cortical thickening or blurring of the gray-white matter junction
Focal epileptiform discharges on EEG corresponding to lesion location

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of dysmorphic neurons without balloon cells plus clinical focal epilepsy and supportive MRI findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires neuropathological examination; MRI and EEG findings support clinical suspicion.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal onset seizures with impaired awareness

common.symptomName: Aura with sensory or autonomic features
searchTerms: aura with sensory or automatic symptoms
pre-seizure sensations involving senses or body functions
sensory or autonomic warning before seizure

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment related to seizure burden
searchTerms: memory and learning issues related to seizures
mild weakness on same side as lesion
mild one-sided weakness on lesion side
loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

rare.symptomName: Developmental delay in early onset cases

imaging: MRI showing focal cortical thickening, blurring of gray-white matter junction, and transmantle sign
FDG-PET hypometabolism in affected cortical region
other: Histopathology revealing dysmorphic neurons without balloon cells

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cortical tubers with balloon cells
Multisystem involvement including skin and renal lesions
Germline mutations in TSC1 or TSC2 genes
Presence of balloon cells on histopathology

redFlags: MRI negative but clinical suspicion remains high
references: Blumcke I, et al. The clinicopathologic spectrum of focal cortical dysplasias: a consensus classification. Epilepsia. 2011 Jun;52(6):158-174.
Wang Y, et al. Somatic MTOR mutations in focal cortical dysplasia type IIa. Ann Neurol. 2016 Feb;79(2):305-315.
International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Classification of Focal Cortical Dysplasia, 2011.
